title: Prairie Avenue 1904: 1808 Prairie's stone front, laid course by course
items: The house beside the Glessner House now has a real stone front: rock-faced limestone laid in courses, each stone its own size and grain, with recessed joints and the odd chipped corner.
Smooth stone trim stands out against the rough wall: a sill under every window, a flat arch of wedge-shaped stones over each opening, two belts and a coping over the base.
The base is two deep-jointed courses, and corner stones on the south side alternate long and short where the stone meets the brick.
